name: timer-widget
comment:overrides: brace-expansion <=5.0.8 has a high-severity DoS advisory (GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895) that bypasses the earlier CVE-2026-14257 mitigation; it supersedes the two ReDoS/OOM advisories this override was originally written for (GHSA-3jxr-9vmj-r5cp, GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg). 5.0.9 is the patched release. The override is still load-bearing and must NOT be dropped as 'probably fixed upstream': the consumers in this tree ask for ^1.1.7 / ^2.0.1 / ^2.0.2 / ^5.0.5 (minimatch under glob, asar, universal, dir-compare, filelist), so without the pin npm resolves vulnerable 1.x and 2.x copies alongside the patched one. It reaches us purely through the electron-builder dev toolchain, never through app runtime code — 'npm audit --omit=dev' is clean either way. 5.0.9 ships dual CJS+ESM exports, so the CJS consumers keep working. @xmldom/xmldom ^0.8.15 (8 advisories incl. GHSA-6gmq-8vp8-gcm6, under plist), fast-uri ^3.1.8 (SSRF/host confusion GHSA-f65p-4m7j-42xc and 3 more, under ajv) and js-yaml ^4.3.2 (GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh) are pinned the same way: all three reach us only through the electron-builder toolchain, but an acceptance scanner reads package-lock/SBOM and flags them regardless. Each pin stays inside the major the consumer asks for — plist 3.x breaks on xmldom 0.9 (mimeType became mandatory).
comment:electronFuses: build.electronFuses (SEC-03): in the packaged binary Electron cannot run as plain Node (runAsNode), ignores NODE_OPTIONS and --inspect, validates app.asar against the hash embedded at build time and loads the app only from it. grantFileProtocolExtraPrivileges stays TRUE on purpose: the windows are served from file://, and with that fuse off their origin is opaque — localStorage throws 'Access is denied for this document' and the control panel dies at startup (measured 2026-09-25 on a fused Electron copy with e2e/windows-load-clean). It can only be turned off together with moving the windows to a custom scheme (protocol.handle), which changes the storage origin and needs a settings migration. resetAdHocDarwinSignature: the mac build is unsigned (identity: null), flipping fuses breaks Electron's stock ad-hoc signature, and arm64 macOS kills unsigned binaries. Tests: tests/release-gates.test.js (config) and scripts/verify-packed.js (reads the bits back from the packed binary in CI).
comment:debDepends: build.deb.depends = electron-builder's default list (it is REPLACED, not extended, by this key) plus libgbm1 and libasound2. Without them `apt install ./TimerWidget-*.deb` succeeds on a clean system and the app then dies at start: 'libasound.so.2: cannot open shared object file' (ubuntu:24.04) and 'libgbm.so.1' (ubuntu:22.04, debian:12) — found 25.09.2026 by the CI job deb-launch-container. Desktop images usually have both, which is why it went unnoticed. ALSA is 'libasound2t64 | libasound2', t64 FIRST: on Ubuntu 24.04 the bare name libasound2 is only virtual, and apt satisfied it with liboss4-salsa-asound2 — an OSS shim without real ALSA symbols ('undefined symbol: snd_device_name_get_hint'); 22.04 and Debian 12 have no t64 package and take the real libasound2.
